item.title: 4-day holiday begins as country gears up for election

item.title: Over 4,81,000 expatriate postal ballots reach ahead of polls
item.description: A total of 4,81,185 expatriate ballots cast through the “Postal Vote BD” mobile application for the 13th National Parliamentary Election and the Referendum 2026 have so far arrived in Bangladesh, election officials said on Wednesday.Meanwhile, 5,15,619 overseas voters have already completed voting using the app. Salim Ahmad Khan, Team Leader of the OCV-SDI project on expatriate voter registration, confirmed the figures while briefing reporters.He said that 7,66,862 ballots registered through the

item.title: CEC to address nation this evening
item.description: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) AMM Nasir Uddin will address the nation on Wednesday evening ahead of the national election scheduled for February 12.According to the EC sources, the speech was recorded on Tuesday evening and will be broadcast simultaneously on Bangladesh Television (BTV), Bangladesh Betar and all private television and radio channels.The CEC is expected to outline the overall preparations for the national election and urge voters to cast their ballots without fear.

item.title: Ballots being sent, Dhaka other major cities to reach this evening
item.description: Preparations for the 13th National Parliament Election and the referendum have entered the final stage, with the dispatch of ballot papers to polling centers across the country now underway.According to the Election Commission's pre-determined plan, ballot boxes will reach major cities, including Dhaka, by Wednesday evening. item.title: Over 2,700 magistrates, nearly 10 lakhs security personnel deployed ahead of polls
item.description: The Election Commission (EC) has appointed a total of 2,098 executive magistrates and 657 judicial magistrates to perform election-related duties for the 13th National Parliamentary Election and the Referendum, scheduled to be held on Thursday.According to the EC, 657 judicial magistrates will remain deployed in 299 constituencies to take cognizance of election-related offences and complete trials. item.title: EC prohibits candidates from using vehicles to ferry voters in polls
item.description: The Election Commission (EC) has barred candidates, election agents, or supporters from using vehicles to transport voters to polling stations during the 13th parliamentary election and the concurrent referendum.The EC issued the directive through a circular signed by Deputy Secretary Monir Hossain, instructing returning officers to ensure that no candidate or supporter violates the code of conduct or engages in voter influence activities.
